content.text:
Sanity check passes overall. The tickets describe real upstream gaps and are correctly linked to SKI-13. No code or Linear changes made.

- [DATA-5](https://linear.app/21n/issue/DATA-5/expose-canonical-namespace-storage-metadata-for-datafn-operations): sound. DataFn currently has a private internal-table registry using `namespace`, while normal resource rows use `__ns`; Skillplane therefore performs catalog discovery. Evidence: [internal-tables.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/superfunctions-dev/datafn/server/src/execution/internal-tables.ts:3) and [concrete-migration.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/skillplane/SKI-13/packages/control-plane/src/concrete-migration.ts:66).

- DATA-5 tightening: define completeness as all namespace-bearing storage derived from the active schema, enabled built-ins/plugins, generated join tables, and DataFn internal tables. Also distinguish table-copy metadata from namespace-level fencing. The permission-directory outbox must drain, while post-quiescence acknowledgements may still update/delete rows; it is not simply “fenced” like ordinary data.

- [DATA-6](https://linear.app/21n/issue/DATA-6/expose-canonical-structural-resource-selector-extraction): strongly justified. DataFn already contains a private structural traversal for internal-resource protection, and Skillplane independently duplicates it. Evidence: [server.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/superfunctions-dev/datafn/server/src/server.ts:211) and [resource-selectors.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/worktrees/skillplane/SKI-13/packages/datafn/src/resource-selectors.ts:1).

- DATA-6 correction: `version` in `DfqlQuery`/`DfqlMutation` is a resource/schema version, not a protocol-envelope version; transactions have no envelope version. Replace `protocolVersion` and “unsupported envelope versions” with an extractor/contract version—or explicitly make introducing protocol versioning a separate requirement. See [dfql.ts](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/superfunctions-dev/datafn/core/src/dfql.ts:11).

- DATA-6 tightening: the API should accept an action/route discriminant plus payload, because query batches, mutation batches, transact wrapped/bare steps, sync push, and cross-resource search have different structural shapes.

Triage hygiene only: both tickets remain unassigned, unprioritized, unlabeled backlog items. Their rationale/delivery documents, PR attachment, and SKI-13 relationship are all present.

Repository validation used live `origin/dev` at `7a711258`; the local checkout itself is 83 commits behind and has unrelated dirty files, which I left untouched.
